intro.title: Nine JEPs. One showcase.
intro.narration: JDK 27 shipped nine JEPs. I built a runnable demo, a test, and a benchmark for every single one. Here is what they measure.

g1.title: G1 is now the default collector everywhere
g1.narration: The G1 collector is now the ergonomic default in every environment — even on a single CPU. No more surprise collector changes in small containers.

headers.title: Compact object headers, measured
headers.narration: Object headers shrank from ninety-six bits to sixty-four. A two-int record now allocates sixteen bytes instead of twenty-four.

tls.title: Post-quantum TLS by default
tls.narration: X25519MLKEM768 is now the most preferred TLS 1.3 key exchange group — quantum-resistant handshakes with zero configuration.

jfr.title: JFR redacts secrets before disk
jfr.narration: JDK 27 redacts sensitive values inside the JVM. A password recorded in a startup event never reaches the recording file.

lazy.title: Lazy constants, at most once
lazy.narration: Lazy constant replaces the holder-class idiom. Computation happens at most once — and failure is permanent, so retries belong inside the supplier.

patterns.title: Primitive patterns, exact by design
patterns.narration: Primitive patterns convert only when the conversion is exact. Forty-two takes the int case, five billion falls to long, and zero point one to double.

scopes.title: Structured concurrency, finally shaped right
scopes.narration: One scope per request, one fork per remote call. The scope is the cancellation boundary — when anything fails, its siblings are cancelled.

orders.title: The measured pipeline
orders.narration: Four orders through three service calls: five hundred seventy milliseconds sequential, two hundred fifty-eight structured — about two point two times faster, with identical results.

vector.title: Vector API: four times faster
vector.narration: A dot product with the Vector API runs about four times faster than the scalar loop, tracking the four SIMD lanes almost exactly.

pem.title: PEM encodings, one line per key
pem.narration: The PEM API encodes keys in one line — including encryption — and deletes every hand-rolled base64 wrapper.

results.title: The receipts
results.narration: Nine JEPs, thirty-three tests, real benchmarks on JDK 27 build thirty-five. All code and numbers are in the repository.

outro.title: Code, tests, benchmarks
outro.narration: Clone the repository, run the tests, and reproduce every number on your own hardware. Thanks for watching.
